top_story.headline: Immigration agency signs sole-source follow-on for court-ordered family reunification after prior contract expired
top_story.dek: Also today: an Army armed-guard order in Iraq posted weeks after work began, and a protest-frozen Fort Carson extension.
paragraphs: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services posted a justification for a sole-source follow-on with the International Organization for Migration to support families reunited under the Miss L. v. Immigration and Customs Enforcement settlement. The previous contract, awarded sole-source in August 2021, ran through September 12, 2026. The value is redacted.

The agency says a lapse would violate the court order and that a 120-day procurement timeline left too little time to compete. The document says responsibility moved from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after a late-fiscal-2025 decision by the Secretary of Homeland Security, with the transfer settled in April 2026.

Separately, the Department of the Army issued a notice to proceed on September 10 to GardaWorld Federal Services for armed guards near Erbil, Iraq, and posted its justification October 8. The Department of the Army also extended base operations at Fort Carson for 60 days with T&H Services LLC while a Government Accountability Office protest holds up the successor contract.

sections.headline: Immigration contractor's court-ordered family reunification work continues through a sole-source follow-on after the prior contract ran out
paragraphs: 25 new sole-source justifications and 603 new solicitations were posted October 8-9; 184 notices already covered in earlier editions are not repeated (7 justifications, 177 solicitations). Two of the eight document-extraction batches failed, so 13 justifications below are judged from titles only.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Immigration agency keeps a sole-source contractor for court-ordered family reunification services
meta: urgent need, no time to compete (document cites 41 U.S.C. 1901)
blocks.text: The follow-on covers help for families reunited under the Miss L. v. Immigration and Customs Enforcement settlement: parole and work-permit applications, travel booking, pre-departure briefings and a help desk. The prior contract, awarded sole-source in August 2021, ran through September 12, 2026; the agency says a lapse would violate the court order and that a 120-day procurement timeline left too little time to compete. The document says administration moved from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services after a late-fiscal-2025 decision by the Secretary of Homeland Security, with the transfer settled in April 2026.

blocks.title: Army orders armed guards for Erbil, Iraq, from GardaWorld and posts the justification weeks after work began
meta: urgent need, skipped competition among existing contract holders
Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command–Rock Island
blocks.text: The order covers armed guard services near Erbil International Airport for U.S. Army Central and the Combined Joint Task Force for Operation Inherent Resolve. The document says the Army issued a notice to proceed on September 10, 2026 and awarded an undefinitized task order under an existing contract, then posted the justification October 8. It says the need left about 20 days to mobilize armed personnel and that GardaWorld was the most immediately executable option.

blocks.title: Fort Carson base operations extended 60 days with the incumbent while a protest freezes the successor contract
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Army, Mission and Installation Contracting Command–Fort Carson
blocks.text: The extension keeps base operations and maintenance running at Fort Carson. The document says a formal Government Accountability Office protest (B-424583) against the successor contract led to a stop-work order on June 15, 2026, and calls the incumbent the only responsible source able to sustain operations during the transition.

blocks.title: NASA gives its longtime collision-avoidance contractor a $47.5 million sole-source award
meta: only one company can do it
National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Goddard Space Flight Center
blocks.text: The award covers orbital safety analysis for conjunction assessment and collision avoidance on NASA missions. The agency says Omitron, Inc. developed the legacy Astrodynamics Support Workstation software and has provided this service since the 1980s, leaving no other source with the specialized expertise.

blocks.title: Homeland Security buys fingerprint-matching software support for its biometric databases from the only vendor with the code
meta: only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security, Office of Procurement Operations
blocks.text: The purchase covers licensing, maintenance and sustainment of fingerprint matching software and hardware for the department's IDENT and HART biometric systems. The justification says the systems are built on proprietary Thales technology whose source code and interfaces are not available to the government or third parties.

sections.headline: $900 million Department of Veterans Affairs award to TriWest Healthcare Alliance leads 18 new awards of $2 million or more
paragraphs: The 25-day sweep found 19 new first-time awards, 18 of them $2 million or more. None were tied to the White House or Executive Office of the President.

blocks.text: TriWest Healthcare Alliance Corp received a $900,485,187 order from the Department of Veterans Affairs on October 7. It is classified as government health insurance programs, and the only description on file is "EXPRESS REPORT: FY26 SEPTEMBER," so the record does not say what services it covers. Award.

Atlantic Diving Supply, Inc. won two call orders from the Department of State, $12,045,581 (September 16) and $4,514,119 (September 18), under a blanket purchase agreement. The descriptions say only that the orders follow an attached spreadsheet and are classified as miscellaneous professional support, so the items bought are not stated. ($12,045,581, $4,514,119).

J G M Property Group, Inc. received $11,501,529 from the Department of Housing and Urban Development on September 30 for field service management in areas 1P and 4P, classified as maintenance of residential buildings. Award.

Crane & Co., Inc. got two October 7 orders from the Bureau of Engraving and Printing for December 2026 currency paper deliveries: $10,479,176 for one fund and $8,769,414 for another, about $19.2 million combined. ($10,479,176, $8,769,414).

ID.me, LLC received an $8,000,000 call order from the General Services Administration on September 28 for identity-verification software as a service; the description references HHS CMS, which appears to point to a Department of Health and Human Services customer. Award.

sections.headline: OMB Conditions $2.9 Billion CBP Apportionment on Hiring Plan Revisions
paragraphs: The Office of Management and Budget approved $2.9 billion in apportionments to the Department of Homeland Security for U.S. Customs and Border Protection personnel and retention bonuses, but with a significant condition: OMB is withholding full approval until the agency finalizes a revised CBP hiring plan that relies on existing funding sources to the greatest extent possible. This represents an oversight hold—a mechanism OMB uses to request additional information on programmatic spending before releasing funds.

blocks.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection received $2.3 billion for personnel (line 6032) and $576 million for retention, hiring, and performance bonuses (line 6033), both under Public Law 119-21 appropriations for fiscal 2027. The footnote on both line items states: "OMB requests additional information on programmatic spending for some or all of the apportioned funds." According to the apportionment documents, DHS will work closely with OMB to finalize the hiring plan using existing sources where possible. Apportionment.

The Corporation for National and Community Service (operating as AmeriCorps) submitted an updated fiscal 2026 spend plan significantly larger than its prior version—652 kilobytes versus 93 kilobytes—indicating material revisions to program allocations. The plan allocates $103.3 million to Volunteers in Service to America, $236.9 million to the National Senior Volunteer Corps, $557.1 million to AmeriCorps State and National operations, and $37.7 million to the National Civilian Community Corps, totaling $975.5 million in operating expenses. While we cannot see a line-by-line diff of what changed from the prior version, the size increase indicates substantial revisions to budget detail or program structure. Spend Plan.
